units.title: Kittering Holm: practical observations for the last days of the contract.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Since the contract is due to end on the 30th, I have opened a short thread for practical observations only: boats, lights, what can actually be seen from the shore. Questions about the owner and its property belong in the other thread. Please give a source, or say plainly that you are guessing. And, once again, no speculation about named members of the crew. Thank you.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What would we expect to see if the job were nearly finished? From Gilliver, the skyline would change at the south end first, because that is where the landing stage is and where any sensible crew starts. On Tuesday's crossing I thought the south shoulder looked thinner than a fortnight ago. I would not put a percentage on it from a ferry rail at nine kilometres, and nor should anyone else.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: From Lisle the Holm sits too low for me to judge its skyline, and I should not like to try without my distance glasses. I can tell you that a former pupil who crews on the morning boat says the contractor's workboat goes out heavy with fuel and comes back with empty drums and skips. That is what a busy site looks like; it says nothing either way about a finished one.

units.author: hist_wiki_marsh
units.text: A small historical footnote, not an argument. The 1890s camp's tally books also record the south shoulder being cleared first, for the same reason: the only decent landing is there. Some things about the Holm are simply geography, and have been for a long time. (Society holdings, ledger B; the relevant pages are summarised on the wiki.)

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Just asking. If it's an ordinary clearance, why has nobody, not the council, not Grieve, not the owners, said what happens on day 31? Thirty days, they told us. That's this week. Then what? Who comes off the island and when? Do your research: count how many went out on the boat at the start and count how many come back. I'm not saying anything. I'm asking.

units.author: skeptic_ferrous
units.text: What happens on day 31 is what happens at the end of every contract I have ever surveyed: the contractor demobilises, the client inspects, and somebody argues about the invoice for six months. Nobody announces it because ordinarily nobody is interested. The absence of a press release is not evidence of anything except the absence of a press office.

units.author: gilliver_lamp
units.text: I can see the island from my back bedroom. The camp lights have been on every night this week, a few of them, and one that moves about whicch I suppose is a torch. I couldnt tell you from here if they have cut half the trees or all of them. I only know they are up late, and that somebody over there is minding the lights.

units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: For what its worth, 10,000 stems in 30 days with a crew of five is about 67 a head a day, every day, no weather days. Thats doable on plantation conifer with a clean extraction route and nothing going wrong. On an island with no roads and a landing stage that only works at half tide, Id be surprised. Not saying they cant. I priced it in week one and didnt fancy it.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Had the creels on the Holm side Tuesday. North end still had a dark stand on the ridge at dusk, or it looked that way against the sky. South end you can see light through it now where you couldnt in the summer. Make of that what you like. I dont know their count and I didnt go close to find out.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: On day 31, legally, nothing changes. The consent is for vegetation clearance, it runs for three years from the decision date, and condition 4 requires a site restoration plan within six months of works ceasing. Whether Grieve finishes by the 30th is a matter between Grieve and its client. The council will not announce anything because there is nothing for it to determine.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: My eldest's class has a sweepstake on whether they finish. I've told him that betting on other people's jobs is rude. He has put 50p on 'nearly'. Unrelated: is the Gilliver boat running on Saturday? We're visiting my aunt and I am not reading eighty posts about trees to find out.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Saturday's Gilliver sailings are in the Ferries and Roads board, pinned this morning. The short answer is yes, normal timetable. I would gently ask that this thread stay on the island, and that the sweepstake stay in your eldest's classroom.

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Lads, it's a tree job. They'll finish or they won't, the company will moan about the bill either way, and in a month you'll all be arguing about bins again. Grow up.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: Doable, he says, on plantation with roads. The Holm has neither. So either they were told something we weren't about the deadline, or the deadline was never the point. Which one is it? Nobody can tell me. Just asking questions, as usual, and as usual getting no answers.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: I might be wrong about this, but the lights on the Holm last night went out in a different order from usual. Usually the big one by the shore goes last. Last night it stayed on until it got light. Probably someone just forgot to switch it off. Sorry, I know that isn't much of an observation.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Big light by the shore will be the one on their jetty, I'd guess. It was on when I went out at half four. Nothing odd in leaving a light on a jetty, I'd leave one myself if I had boats coming in the morning.

units.title: Ardent Vale 'other properties' list: two entries withdrawn.
units.author: propwatch_ledger

edit.text: Findings, revised. (1) I am withdrawing entries 3 and 5 from the list I posted on Sunday (not Monday, as I first wrote). Entry 3, the upland estate, belongs to a different company with a similar name, which I should have checked. Entry 5, the former radar site, was sold to a wind developer. (2) Entries 1, 2 and 4 stay: all three were bought through the same intermediary agent. (3) I apologise to anyone who repeated 3 and 5.

units.text: Findings, revised. (1) I am withdrawing entries 3 and 5 from the list I posted on Monday. Entry 3, the upland estate, belongs to a different company with a similar name, which I should have checked. Entry 5, the former radar site, was sold to a wind developer, not to Ardent Vale. (2) I am keeping entries 1, 2 and 4, which still go back to the same intermediary agent. (3) I apologise to anyone who repeated 3 and 5.

units.author: truthwatch_gil
units.text: So two were wrong, fine, but the other three are all remote and all bought through the same agent. That is the pattern. Withdrawing two doesn't make the rest go away. I said at the weekend it was a network of private refuges and I stand by most of that, whatever the other post said.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: For the record: on one day you wrote that the list proves the refuge theory, and on the next you wrote that the list was probably planted to discredit it. Both posts are still up. I am not removing anything. I am only asking members to read them side by side before quoting either.

units.author: propwatch_ledger
units.text: Gil, I'd be careful with 'pattern'. Three properties bought through one agent is what agents are for. My finding is narrow: the same agent, three purchases, about eleven months apart. I don't know what any of the properties are for and I have never said so. I would rather be dull and right than interesting and wrong twice.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Housekeeping of my own: this thread was moved to Local Oddities at one member's request and back to General at another's. It is staying in General. It is about filings, and I would like it to stay about filings.

units.author: hollow_signal

edit.text: ...you withdrew the two that were getting too close. Interesting. I said weeks ago that the boats would stop after the thirtieth. Read back. I won't be posting much longer, and some of you will understand why.

units.text: ...you withdrew the two that were getting too close. Interesting choice. I've said too much on this board already and I won't be posting much longer. Watch the boats after the thirtieth, that's all.

units.author: morrow_unknown
units.text: Sorry to butt in. Hollow, you edited that post about twenty minutes after you wrote it. The first version didn't say the boats would stop, it only said to watch them, and it didn't say you'd said it weeks ago. I'm not trying to start anything. I just think people reading later should know it changed.

units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: Believe what you like about my edits. The record will speak when it needs to. This is my last word on this board, and probably anywhere else. Some of you were kind. Most of you weren't listening.

units.title: Rope Walk recycling: the outage-week backlog.
units.author: sb_bins
units.text: The council newsletter of the 22nd promised that all collections affected by 'Sound Power works' would be caught up within seven days. It is now the 28th. The green boxes on Rope Walk have been out since the 19th and the gulls have opened two of them. I have photographed both and the newsletter. Bernard (Rope Walk)

units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: Weyhaven has the same problem and we didn't even have the outages on our side of the city. The crews went to four-day weeks in spring and nobody told the residents. You'll get yours Thursday if they follow the city pattern, which they won't, because nothing in this region follows a pattern except the 38 bus, which is always early.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Bernard, I have passed your photographs to the council's waste team, as you asked. They are answering the contact form within two working days, I am told. The gulls are beyond my powers as a moderator.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Tollinby is the same. Ours came at 6am on Sunday, which I didn't know they did, and took the glass but not the cardboard. The kids have built a fort out of the cardboard. It's very good actually, it has a door and a sign. It is also in the hall, where I keep walking into it.

units.title: Brackwater junction, now that the roadworks are 'finished'.
units.author: sb_roadworks
units.text: Update for anyone on the Tollinby road: temp lights gone, new surface down, and the junction is now a give-way with a hedge exactly where you need to look right. Sat behind a tractor for six minutes while it worked up the courage. Two weeks late and somehow worse. Classic B-road engineering.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: At least you have a road. The 07:10 from Lisle left at 07:10 this morning for the first time in a month and I nearly missed it out of habit, standing on the slip with my coffee like an idiot while it pulled away on time.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: We had a crew at that junction last week resetting the pole-top switch. The hedge belongs to the estate, not the council, so that's who to ask. They're very nice about it on the phone. They just don't cut it.

units.author: brackwater_keeper
units.text: The estate cuts that hedge in February, outside nesting season, as the law asks. If drivers took that junction at a sensible speed they'd not need to see round a hedge. Same goes for the ones who use the reservoir lane as a racetrack after dark.

units.title: Pebble update: officially an indoor cat now.
units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Hello all, a little Pebble news since so many of you ask after her. (Grey, one white sock, you'll remember.) She has decided she is an indoor cat after dark. She sits by the back door at dusk, looks out for a long moment, and walks away. In daylight she is out in the yard as usual. The vet says she is perfectly healthy. Thank you again to Mrs Garrow for the shed.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Our cat did exactly that after fireworks night two years ago and it wore off by spring. Our vet's advice: put a litter tray by the back door, don't make a fuss, and let her decide. Cats like to think it was their idea.

units.author: sb_lostcat
units.text: Thank you, that's kind and very sensible. The tray is down. She has also started sleeping on the landing instead of on the bed, facing the stairs, which I am choosing not to read anything into. Thank you to everyone who messaged, and to you especially.

units.title: Carrow Point station, 28th.
units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Readings 07:00: pressure 1031 hPa and rising slowly, wind NNE 6 knots, dew point minus 1, visibility 28,000 m, the Holm as crisp as a paper cut-out. Ground frost on the lawn, the first of the month. After last week's rain this is the high the Met Office has been promising since Tuesday, and for once they're right. More this evening.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Evening: 1033 hPa, wind fallen to near calm, 2.4 degrees and dropping. Clear sky, every star out. If you want to see across to the Holm, tonight is as good as visibility gets. I could make out the camp lights from the garden without the binoculars. Expect a hard frost inland by dawn.

units.title: Trades & Jobs: felling and plant operator available from the 31st
units.author: trades_holm_work
units.text: Bumping my ticket list one more time: felling small and large trees, aerial rescue, tracked chipper, 13 tonne excavator, own van and insurance. If Grieve's lot come back on the 31st looking for local subcontract work, or anyone needs a big hedge down before winter, message me. Glad I didnt go out there in the end, the way folk are talking, but Id hire anyone who did.

units.author: sb_mod
units.text: A reminder that Trades & Jobs posts may be bumped once a week. This is the second bump in five days. I will leave it up, as the board is quiet and the tickets are at least listed clearly.

units.author: skeptic_planner
units.text: If you want work after the Holm, look at the Brackwater estate's woodland management plan, which went in last month: thinning across 40 hectares over two winters, contractor not yet named. The application is on the council portal under the estate's name, decision due in about five weeks.

units.title: Found: child's blue mitten, Lisle ferry slip.
units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Found on the rail of the Lisle slip at 07:05: a child's blue knitted mitten with a white star on the back, threaded on a string so it must have come off a coat. Handed in at the pier office. The 07:10 was on time, so I had exactly four minutes to be a good citizen and I used them.

units.author: retired_teacher
units.text: That will belong to one of the Pryor children, I expect; their grandmother knits those stars for the whole family. I shall tell her it is at the pier office. Thank you for handing it in rather than leaving it on the rail. Things left on rails tend to end up in the Sound.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Collected at 17:40 by a very serious six-year-old, the pier office tells me. They also say it's the third mitten this month and they now keep a box for them behind the ticket window.

units.title: Ferries & Roads: Saturday sailings, normal timetable.
units.author: sb_mod
units.text: Pinned at members' request. Sound Lines confirms that Saturday's Port Ammet, Lisle and Gilliver sailings run to the normal timetable, including the 22:40 night crossing with the new deck lighting. Please check the operator's bulletin on the morning itself, though the Met Office says fog is unlikely this week.

units.author: sb_commuter_lisle
units.text: Fog unlikely, they say, after the month we've had. I'll believe it when the 07:10 goes at 07:10 two days running. It did today. I am not getting excited about it.

units.author: parent_tollinby
units.text: Found it, thank you. Saturday 10:15 out to Gilliver, 16:40 back, aunt has been told, sandwiches are planned. The kids are already arguing about who gets the window seat on a boat that is mostly windows.

units.title: Housekeeping: month end, and a few reminders
units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: (1) The 'edge of the light' discussion stays in the merged thread, please, not a new thread every night. (2) If you're on the last week of a rota, tell us how it went; we like those. (3) A glass of water and a stretch before you post anything at 4am that you wouldn't post at noon. (4) Thank you to everyone who reported the spam accounts this week. Be kind to each other.

units.author: lh_baker_coriveth
units.text: Re (3): water is good but a heel of warm bread is better. Rye tonight, with caraway, because the owner has decided we are fancy now. The whole shop smells like a field after rain. First trays out at four.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: Re (2): last week of nights for me before a fortnight of days. A&E's been calmer since the power settled. Only two 'fell over in the dark' tonight, both on the car park steps where the bulb's gone. Reported the bulb. Third time. Big news on the run: the vending machine on level 2 now takes cards.

units.author: lh_nurse_halvard
units.text: Congratulations on the machine. Ours still eats coins and gives back a single mint, like a tip. Quiet ward tonight, three empty beds, which the night sister treats as a personal insult and keeps checking in case someone's hiding in one. Back to it.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping, appended: the rye is approved by the moderation team. Water remains mandatory, and so does sleep when you get home, however good the bread was.

units.title: The corridor lights did it again (short, I'm tired)
units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: ok so: last night at 02:15 the corridor sensor lights came on one by one from the lift end toward my lab door, exactly like before facilities 'fixed' it. Nobody arrived. I didn't get up. I have a methods chapter due Thursday and I genuinely do not have the energy to be scared. Logging it here so I remember it happened, and then going back to my plots.

units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Same islands, other side of town. Ours did nothing all night except one customer buying eleven bananas. I asked what for. He said 'a recipe' and left. Respect to the chapter.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: If it's the same sequence as before the repair, ask facilities whether they replaced the sensors or only the controller. A cascade of corridor lights usually means one trigger and a daisy chain: a draught, a moth on a lens, a door settling. n of 1, and you are exhausted. Write the chapter, then email facilities.

units.author: lh_insomniac_tollinby
units.text: There is a line in an old novel about a house that lit its lamps for a guest who never came, and a housekeeper who laid a place anyway, every night, without complaint. I always liked the housekeeper best. Good luck with Thursday.

units.title: Edge of the light, one more time: what the reports share (and don't)
units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: I've gone back over the merged thread: twenty-odd reports since the 17th. What they share: the person is tired, alone, in the last third of a shift, looking out of a lit space into an unlit one. What they don't share: height, clothing, how long, how far. That is what a perception effect plus a forum looks like. Once someone names a shape, everyone's peripheral vision has a template. I'm not calling anyone a liar. I'm saying the pattern is us.

units.author: lh_dockguard_coriveth
units.text: Patrolled 04:00 local, nil found. For the record my camera report from last week turned out to be a fox, as I posted. Take mine out of your twenty. That's one.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: Thank you. That is the most useful post this thread has had. If three more people did the same honest subtraction we would have a real number instead of a feeling, and I'd happily argue about the real number.

units.author: lh_lighttender_tamsin
units.text: That is fair, and I have said much the same to myself on the gallery at three in the morning. I would add one thing the reports share that you didn't list: in none of them does the figure come into the light. Perhaps that is also part of the template. I keep the gallery door shut now, and I don't think that makes me a believer. It makes me a man who likes a shut door.

units.author: lh_miner_vellmark
units.text: Old lads at the pit say keep to the lamp. They said it before forums. Before phones. Before me. I don't say they're right. I say it's older than your template. On the bus now. Frost on the inside of the window.

units.author: skeptic_orla
units.text: Older doesn't mean truer, though. 'Keep to the lamp' is exactly what you'd tell someone in a mine with shafts in it, or on a cliff path, or a dock. The good advice survives and a story grows round it to make people remember it. Source: twelve years of watching call-ins turn safety advice into legends in about a fortnight.

units.title: Break-time menu, week four
units.author: lh_picker_weyhaven
units.text: Break at 02:30. Menu: two cereal bars, coffee from the machine that says hot chocolate on every button, and a satsuma I found in my coat from last week. Target tonight is 160 an hour and the scanner on lane 9 keeps logging me out mid-pick. If I disappear, I'm in a tote.

units.author: lh_carer_vellmark
units.text: Toast for the residents who wake at three, and a slice for me. Mrs P asks for hers cut into triangles, 'like a hotel'. The intercom has been quiet all week, and I find I miss it a little, which I know is silly. Sorry, that's not a menu.

units.author: lh_security_st
units.text: Cold pasta from a tub and a flask of tea, patrol route C, Control on the radio asking if I've 'eyes on the far bay' every half hour like the far bay is going somewhere. Car park's half empty since the outages stopped. People got used to shopping in daylight, I reckon, and haven't switched back.

units.author: lh_porter_portammet
units.text: A satsuma from the coat pocket is a delicacy on the run. We have a yoghurt in the staff fridge dated two months ago that nobody will throw out, because throwing it out means admitting it's yours. It has become a sort of mascot.

units.author: lh_taxi_halvard
units.text: last week of nights for me too, I've probably said. fare tonight paid in coins counted out on the armrest one at a time, then asked if I'd wait while he checked his front door was locked. I waited. it was locked. he waved. anyway, menu: cheese sandwich, the end

units.title: A note before I go
units.author: hollow_signal
units.text: To the few who understood: the thirtieth is not an ending. The people who planned the Holm have planned others, and the edge of the light is the edge they mean. I can't say more without consequences for people I care about. I'm closing this account tonight. Watch the boats. Watch the lamps in Gilliver.

units.author: lh_mod
units.text: Housekeeping: I've removed the post above. Hinting at insider knowledge about real plans, with nothing behind it, isn't what Lamp Hours is for, and we've asked before. If you are leaving, go well, and get some sleep. Thread closed.

units.title: Forecourt man, an update nobody asked for
units.author: lh_convenience_kestrel
units.text: Forecourt update. The man at the edge of the light was back last night, in the new coat. Stood there 01:40 until about 02:30. A car came. He got in. So he is a man who waits for lifts, which is what I said before. I'm still not sure it's the same man; the coat is very different. He did not buy anything. Rude.

units.author: lh_student_kestrel
units.text: this is the most Kestrel thing I've ever read. a man waits outside a shop for fifty minutes in the cold and does not buy a single steamed bun. I'd have bought three. I'd have bought the shop.

units.author: skeptic_dmitra
units.text: 'A car came. He got in.' I would like that sentence framed and hung above the merged thread. Thank you for following up; most people never come back to say the boring ending.

units.title: Script of the week (utilities helpline edition)
units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: New script line from management: 'I understand that an outage can feel unsettling.' I have now said it 41 times tonight. Most callers want to know when the freezer is safe. One man wanted to know whether he should keep a candle in the window until the power's back. I told him our outage map refreshes every fifteen minutes, which is true and also not an answer. He kept the candle.

units.author: lh_kennel_orrin
units.text: Our clinic's hold music is a pan-pipe version of a lullaby. Clients have started humming it at the front desk. One basset, Juniper, howls along with it in tune, which is more than I can say for our receptionist. Juniper goes home tomorrow and the waiting room will be poorer for it.

units.author: lh_callcentre_tamsin
units.text: Pan-pipes. You poor soul. Ours is a synth loop that repeats every 38 seconds with a little hiccup at the join. I hear the hiccup in my sleep. Juniper is a better singer than anyone in my team meeting, and probably a better manager.

units.author: lh_trucker_orrin
units.text: Advice from the road: when the script won't help, read the caller the weather. Nobody hangs up on the weather. Prairie's clear as a bell tonight, frost on the trailer doors, and the coffee at the 112 stop is fresh for once, which I'm logging as the event of the week.

units.title: The lift (and why I am using it)
units.author: dc_7_irena
units.text: Dear neighbours, I wish to say, so that nobody worries when they see me, that I have started using the lift even when it smells of the bins. My husband would have laughed, because I have walked those stairs for thirty-one years. I am not saying anything about the stairwell. I am only saying that my knees and I have come to an arrangement. Irena, 7C

units.author: dc_5_lorna
units.text: oh Irena love nobody would think a thing of it, I take the lift myself now after a shift if it's still dark and I sit in the lobby with a cup if the light's not up yet, the stairs will be there in daylight and so will we, you take that lift and hold your nose

units.author: dellow_manager
units.text: Kerrow Estates notice ref DC/LIFT/0412. The lift odour has been attributed to a failed seal on the refuse chute hopper at level 8. A replacement seal has been ordered. Residents are reminded that all refuse must be bagged and tied before disposal. We thank residents for their patience.

units.author: dellow_admin
units.text: Thanks for the reference number. For anyone wondering, 'ordered' last time meant five weeks. I'll chase it on Monday. And Irena, you take the lift whenever you like. It's your lift, you pay the service charge. Bev, DCRA

units.author: skeptic_brisk
units.text: Taking the lift is the first sensible thing anyone's said on this board in a month. No offence meant, Irena. The rest of you could learn from her.

units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Irena's choice isn't evidence of anything and nobody here said it was. It's also not your business, since you don't live here. For the thread's purposes: lift use is up, stair use is down, and that is all the data shows. Nothing follows from it.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Irena, I'll put a pine block in the lift tomorrow, the shop has a box left from the summer. If you want shopping brought up, ring the shop bell and my nephew will carry it. Kerrow's seal will come when it comes. H

units.title: Treadmill theory against the times people heard things
units.author: dc_9_tobin
units.text: Since the treadmill came up, I've put the 31 report times from the stairwell threads into a list. By hour: 23-00, 6. 00-01, 9. 01-02, 8. 02-03, 5. 05-06, 1. Daytime, 2 (Irena, Wendell). Garrick, when do you run? I'm not accusing anyone of anything. I need the number.

units.author: dc_6_jordie
units.text: lol tobin made a pivot table of our fear. respect. for the record i floated the treadmill thing half joking, garrick's the one who said it carries through the riser. if he runs at midnight i'm retracting all my jokes and buying him a protein shake

units.author: dc_14_ivy
units.text: (I'm one of the 01-02 ones, I think, unless I'm one of the 02-03 ones; I don't check the clock when I'm drawing.) A treadmill on 10 wouldn't explain the bit where the steps go up past 14. There's no 15. There's the roof door and a lot of cold air.

units.author: dc_10_garrick
units.text: Morning legends, quick one before clients. I went back through the thread like Tobin asked. I run 05:00 to 05:40, every day, that's it. Most of your reports are after midnight and before three. So it's not me, mate. Or not most of it. Maybe the one at five. Sorry. I genuinely wanted it to be me.

units.title: Parking behind block B (again)
units.author: dc_3_wendell
units.text: The white van is back in the disabled bay behind block B. Third time this week. I have its number. I have also reported the 38 for running four minutes early past the Dellow Road stop, which leaves people stood in the cold for the next one. Somebody in this building has to keep track of real problems.

units.author: dc_2_hassan
units.text: Wendell, the white van is my bread supplier. He's there 05:40 to 05:55. I have asked him to use the loading bay and he says there is a car in the loading bay. The car is yours. H

units.title: The prank night and the other nights
units.author: ferry_skipper_odell
units.text: Now the lad's owned up, for the log. His night was the 7th, in fog: he stood at the top of the Gilliver slipway in his granddad's long coat for a dare. My crew's sighting was the 4th, three nights earlier, and Kerris put the figure at the water's edge, not the top. So his story explains his night. It does not explain mine. Added a note to the log, carried on.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: From the engine room: on the 4th I was below nursing the port genset, so I saw nothing. I've worked with Odell and Kerris for nine years and neither of them is a storyteller. A lad in a coat at the top of the ramp is a lad in a coat. A grown person at the waterline who won't answer a hail is a different job.

units.author: ferry_mate_kerris
units.text: Thanks, Skipper. Same as I said on the 5th: tall, dark coat, no light, standing still at the end where the water starts, hailed twice on the loud-hailer. A seventeen-year-old in a big coat at the top of the ramp is a different picture. I'm not angry at the lad. I'm angry at the people who think his night settles all of them.

units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Thank you, Captain Odell. As I've said, the matter of the 7th is closed with the young person's family and I'd ask members to leave him be now. I have nothing to add about the other dates. Byelaw 14 applies to everyone: no access to slipways after dark without good cause. Thank you.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Kerris nobody on here thinks it settles everything. One night explained the rest not. That's where it sits lads and it can sit there. Anyone wanting to argue the rest of it take it to the Sound Board.

units.author: lisle_crew_ada
units.text: Mine was the 10th, at Lisle, and he couldn't have been at both... obviously. Ha. I'm on the day job at the bakery now so I'm not on the slip at night any more. I still don't know what I saw. It's easier not knowing from behind a bread counter, if that makes sense.

units.author: gilliver_teen
units.text: yeah it was the 7th. only the 7th. I know people want it to be every time but it wasn't, I was at my nan's in Port Ammet on the 4th and there are photos with the date on. I'm not doing any more of this. I've said sorry to Mr Quill and to the ferry office and I meant it.

units.title: Contractor's supply vessel: berth 3, 29th and 30th
units.author: harbourmaster_quill
units.text: Notice to harbour users: the contractor's supply vessel will use berth 3 on the mornings of the 29th and 30th for loading. Please keep the berth and the pontoon approach clear from 06:00 on both days. Any questions to the harbour office, please. Thank you.

units.author: ferry_engineer_seth
units.text: Their boat's a tidy old workboat with a knuckle crane on the foredeck. Skipper's from up the coast, not one of ours. I asked him about the Holm landing stage on Monday. He said it's 'fine at half tide, awful at low', which is what everyone says about every landing stage ever built.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: She was low in the water going out this morning. Diesel, I'd guess, by the drums on deck. Came back with skips and empties. Nobody said how many trips are left and I didn't ask. It's their business, not mine.

units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: Berth 3 means berth 3 lads. Last time someone left a punt tied on the pontoon and their skipper sat off the wall twenty minutes waiting. If it's yours shift it tonight or I'll shift it for you and you won't like where.

units.author: fisher_bram
units.text: Out at four. Light on the Holm jetty still burning. Calm as glass, you could hear a generator going over there if you cut the engine. I didn't sit long. Creels were light, prices will be up Friday.

units.title: Weather's turned at last
units.author: harbour_admin
units.text: High pressure sat on us till Sunday at least according to the Met lads. Flat calm at the harbour mouth this morning and frost on the pontoon so mind your feet. Chandlery has de-icer and grit in, cost plus a bit, ask at the counter.

units.author: wx_carrowpoint
units.text: Confirming from the station: 1031 hPa at 07:00 and climbing, minus 1.8 on the gatepost thermometer at dawn. The sea hasn't cooled with the air yet, so expect sea smoke in the creeks first thing while the wind stays off. Pretty, and slippery underfoot.

units.author: lineman_tess
units.text: Thank you, weather. Day shifts start Monday for me, and I'm told my first job is a whole day up a pole in the sunshine replacing insulators. I never thought I'd be this glad about insulators.

units.title: Thanks, and a request
units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: Thanks to everyone who messaged after I went quiet. To repeat what I said yesterday: the phone went into the reservoir at the north inlet, I stayed at my brother's in Tollinby for a few days, everything is fine. I'd be grateful if people stopped asking why I packed up early on the 24th. I've no file of it and nothing to add. Make of it what you will.

units.author: hobby_binaural
units.text: Headphones off for this one, just a hello. Glad you're back and dry. I have a spare handheld in a drawer if your phone's still at the bottom of the reservoir; it's yours for the asking, no strings, no questions.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: ok so I'll say it here once and then stop: really glad you're ok. I sat in the reservoir car park on the 25th with a flask like an idiot. Your car was there, the keeper said it'd been there two nights. I'm not asking. I just. Yeah. Glad.

units.author: tern_audio
units.text: Typo patrol on my own post: the flask was tea, before anyone asks, and 'like an idiot' was about me, not about him.

units.author: lowband_mod
units.text: Pinned for a week. Folks, the man has asked. Questions about the 24th will be removed without comment. Questions about kit, gain settings and his dawn chorus files are very welcome, as always.

units.author: dunlin_rec
units.text: That's kind, thank you. I have a recorder; it was only the phone that went in. I've ordered a waterproof pouch, which my brother has pointed out is the obvious lesson, several times, over breakfast.

units.title: Harbour hum: where I've got to
units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Status on the Gilliver harbour clip. I said I'd found the pump, then I said the pump was off that night. Since then I've checked the ice plant (off), the chandlery chiller (on, but about 20 Hz too high), and two moored boats on shore power (one had a fridge running, close-ish, wrong harmonics). Still not placed. It's a pump somewhere. I just don't know whose.

units.author: skeptic_hollis
units.text: Quick analysis of your posted spectrum: fundamental near 47 Hz, strong odd harmonics. That's small reciprocating compressor, not a centrifugal pump. A domestic fridge would fit, or anything with a fridge in it. Look for something on shore power within a few hundred metres, and check whether the hum cycles: fridges run on and off.

units.author: hobby_hydrophone
units.text: Moorings list is boats only and I've been through it. I'll check the clip for on-off cycling. If it cycles every twenty minutes that's a fridge, and I'll buy whoever owns it a pint for the trouble.
